Title
Research
Description
How we turn bold ideas into tangible results
HKUST Engineering Develops High-Resolution Bionic Eye
A research team led by Prof. FAN Zhiyong has developed a high-resolution bionic eye that integrates full-color imaging, an aberration-corrected field of view exceeding 160 degrees, and event-driven motion detection.
Learn More
HKUST Engineering Researchers Develop Low-Cost Elastocaloric Refrigerant Structure with Over 100-Million-Cycle Fatigue Life
Prof. SUN Qingping’s research team has manufactured a low-cost, ultra-durable elastocaloric refrigerant structure inspired by the stacked porous architecture of honeycombs that operated for more than 100 million cooling cycles with an estimated service life of over 10 years.
Learn More
HKUST Engineering Develops Dynamic Integrated Interface Engineering for Lithium Metal Batteries
Prof. SHAO Minhua has developed a dynamic integrated interface engineering strategy that enhances the energy density and stability of anode-free lithium metal batteries by reconfiguring key battery interfaces.
Learn More
HKUST Engineering Develops Embodied Robotic Arm “EmArm” with Human-Like Touch Sensing
Prof. SHEN Yajing’s team has developed an Embodied Sensorimotor Robotic Arm (EmArm) capable of whole-arm tactile sensing and adaptive manipulation.
Learn More
HKUST Engineering Develops Self-Sustaining Seawater-to-Hydrogen System
Prof. SHANG Chii and his collaborators have developed a sustainable integrated seawater-to-hydrogen system that can produce hydrogen directly from seawater while converting waste heat from electrolysis into a resource for producing the purified water required for hydrogen production.
Learn More
HKUST Engineering Develops Novel Cartilage-Inspired Polymer Nanocoating to Substantially Extend Battery Lifespan
Prof. CHEN Guohua's research team has developed a biomimetic nanocoating that could significantly extend the lifespan of batteries used in smartphones, electric vehicles, and other electronic devices.
Learn More
HKUST Engineering Develops Breakthrough Liquid-Metal Smart Patch for Clinical-Grade At-Home Cardiorespiratory Monitoring
Prof. Hnin Yin Yin NYEIN’s team has developed a novel wearable device named “HELP” (heteromodal epidermal liquid-metal patch). By leveraging liquid-metal technology, this soft, skin-like patch simultaneously tracks both breathing and heart activity.
Learn More
World’s First Zero-Degradation Elastocaloric Cooling Device to Revolutionize Sustainable Refrigeration Technology
Prof. SUN Qingping’s team has unveiled the world’s first zero-degradation elastocaloric cooling device. Powered by a fatigue-resistant, solid-state refrigerant, this innovation delivers durable and green cooling, maintaining its stable performance even over a stunning one million operational cycles.
Learn More
HKUST Engineering Develops Optimization Framework for Autonomous Materials Experimentation Platforms
Prof. YANG Jinglei and Prof. DUAN Molong’s research team has developed a new modeling and optimization framework that helps researchers design modularized autonomous experimentation platforms for new materials by determining the optimal combination of equipment before construction begins.
Learn More
HKUST Engineering Charts a Roadmap for Agentic 7G AI-Powered Wireless Networks
Prof. Khaled B. LETAIEF’s research team proposed a new Reasoning-Empowered Task-Oriented Communication framework that enables AI agents to determine what information to share, when communication is necessary, and why a communicate should occur. The research could pave the way for collective intelligence in future 7G wireless networks.
Learn More
HKUST Engineering Develops “One-Pot” 30-Minute High-Sensitivity At-Home Testing
Prof. HSING I-Ming’s research team developed an innovative “one-pot” testing platform, known as TEMPO, that could transform highly sensitive nucleic acid testing from a laboratory-based procedure into a simple, single-step test that can be performed at home.
Learn More
HKUST Engineering Study Reveals Inter-City Collaboration on Emission Reduction Boosts Sustainability Performance
A large-scale international study led by Prof. LU Mengqian has revealed that inter-city collaboration on emission reduction can improve overall sustainability performance by more than 10%.
Learn More
HKUST Engineering Pioneers Novel Water Purification Technology for Selective Pollutant Polymerization
The research team led by Prof. Irene LO has achieved a major breakthrough by discovering a novel oxidant-free electrocatalytic mechanism, opening up a new direction for water purification technologies.
Learn More
HKUST Engineering Develops Generalist-Specialist Collaboration AI Framework for Disease Diagnosis
Prof. CHEN Hao’s research team has developed a novel AI framework, the Generalist–Specialist Collaboration, which enables a generalist foundation model and specialist models to collaborate on disease diagnosis.
Learn More
HKUST Engineering Develops Ultra-Robust Acoustic Chip Technology to Advance 6G and Satellite Communications
Prof. YANG Yansong’s research team has developed a novel chip architecture that enables the miniature acoustic devices inside smartphones to withstand over 12 times higher power loads while maintaining cooler and more stable operation.
Learn More
HKUST Engineering Improves Solar Cell Performance and Durability Through Molecular Interface Engineering
A research team led by Prof. LIN Yen-Hung has contributed to two recently published studies that show molecular interface engineering can unlock major gains in the efficiency and durability of next-generation perovskite tandem solar cells.
Learn More
HKUST Researchers Develop GenAI Framework for Misalignment-Resistant Virtual Staining to Accelerate Histopathology Workflows
A research team from the School of Engineering has developed a novelGenAI framework that can produce high-fidelity virtually stained images even when training image pairs are imperfectly aligned, paving the way for faster and more tissue-saving histopathology workflows.
Learn More
